company: Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile S.A.
market_holds: Spot 51.835 (sealed baseline 2026-11-17 18:08 UTC), -4.8% over 5 days, -13.7% over 20 days, -45.6% from the 52-week high and 1.4% above the 52-week low. Front-expiry straddle 6.99%, event-implied 6.01%, but the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so treat it as indicative only. Put/call open interest is 0.26 on just 1,247 contracts. Short interest is under 1% of float (Equibles, about 0.85% on 2026-10-01), so there is no squeeze set-up. Consensus per Earnings Whispers (2026-11-10): EPS $1.94 and revenue $2.26B, both down sequentially from Q2's $2.31 and $2.47B. Benzinga lists a higher $2.17 and $2.34B, so the bar itself is uncertain. Guide: Q3 lithium volumes about equal to Q2's record of 84k t LCE. The market plainly holds the collapse in China lithium carbonate, which is public every day: about CNY 159k/t on 2026-09-01, below 123k by 2026-09-18, about 100k in mid-October and 89,050 today, a one-year low (Trading Economics). Albemarle already guided Q4 lower on 2026-11-04. JPMorgan cut its target from $88 to $71 on 2026-11-06 because of lower near-term earnings. The last open reactions were modest: Q1 2026 (EPS about $1.28 against $1.78 consensus) opened -3.0% and then closed +4.4% on the call; Q2 2026 (a 14% beat) opened flat at 75.36 against 75.38 and gained on the call day. Both from my own read of Yahoo daily bars.
view: Q3 is a backward-looking quarter whose prices were set before the September-November collapse. The Chilean reference price (Banco Central / Cochilco, FOB South America) averaged about 19.9 in July, about 19.7 in August and 19.4 in September (US$/kg). In Q2 it was roughly 19.2 / 21.7 / 20.8, and SQM realised $21.80 in Chile against that. So Q3 realised prices should be about 4-7% lower, a smaller drop than the roughly 8.5% fall in revenue that the Earnings Whispers consensus implies. Chilean customs exports of carbonate were 23.4k / 24.1k / 18.9k t over July-September, which fits the guide of flat volumes. My own rough arithmetic puts Q3 revenue at about $2.35-2.40B and EPS at about $2.0-2.15: a beat against the $1.94 bar, in line against Benzinga's $2.17. Peer read-across points the same way. Albemarle 'beat a lowered bar' and guided Q4 lower, and it still opened +4.8% (94.97 to 99.56 on 2026-11-05), though it has since given all of that back and more (88.07 today) as spot kept falling. Against that: the release only carries numbers and CEO commentary on demand. Price guidance for Q4 comes on the call at 10:00 ET on 11-18, after the scored open. SQM's open has reacted little to its numbers (flat on a 14% beat in Q2), and the overhang, a Q4 realised price likely in the mid-teens, is already visible to everyone. Net: a slight upward lean from a probable modest beat on a beaten-down stock. It is not enough to recommend.
unpriced: Possibly a small gap. The lower consensus ($1.94/$2.26B) seems to assume a steeper Q3 realised-price drop than the Chilean reference series shows (about -5% against about -8.5% on revenue). But the true bar is uncertain (Benzinga $2.17), and SQM's open has historically priced the numbers only mildly. Not a confident gap.

recommendation.reason: Q3 realised prices look only about 5% below Q2 on the Chilean reference series, which points to a modest beat against the lower consensus. But the consensus sources disagree (EPS $1.94 against $2.17). The Q4 price collapse is public and well absorbed, and SQM's open moved little even on a 14% beat last quarter. The probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 Chile realised price at or below about $19.5/kg, or lithium volume well under 84k t, would make it a miss against even the lower bar and push the open down; an explicit release statement of a sharply lower Q4 price would do the same.

self_critique: The beat case rests on the Earnings Whispers consensus, which may be stale or low; Benzinga's $2.17 would make my estimate in line. Iodine (25-30% of profit) may have softened, as management flagged easing toward year-end, and I could not check it. China spot is making new lows on the run day itself, and ALB's pop faded entirely, so any Q4 commentary in the release could swamp a Q3 beat. The open has historically barely priced SQM's numbers, so even a correct beat call may land inside the deadband.
approach_notes: The 'freshest data first' rule and 'rebuild the line yourself' paid: the Chilean reference price series gave a dated Q3 price read independent of consensus. The window rule mattered: the call comes after the scored open, so last quarters' open-only reactions mattered more than the implied move.
